content:
This week, Apple has continued to steadily expand its Apple Sports app, further strengthening soccer coverage and providing tennis fans with new ways to track major tournaments. Here are the details of this update.

Apple Sports adds new soccer leagues and tennis schedules

When the Apple Sports app first launched, the experience was quite limited in terms of both supported regions and the sports it covered.

Since then, the app has made progress in both areas — its availability has expanded to over 170 countries and regions, while it continues to add new sports, leagues, and tournaments.

For example, earlier this year Apple Sports expanded to 90 new countries and rolled out multiple features centred on the FIFA World Cup.

This week, Apple Sports has been updated again, adding the Australian A-League Men, Egyptian Premier League, Israeli Premier League, and South African Premier League to its soccer lineup.

In addition, the app now lets tennis fans "follow live draws... including brackets for Grand Slam and 1000-level events," Apple says, allowing users to "see matchups and results for each round at a glance."

Here are the full release notes for Apple Sports 4.4:

Soccer coverage continues to expand with the addition of the Australian A-League Men, Egyptian Premier League, Israeli Premier League, and South African Premier League. Tennis fans can now use Apple Sports to follow live draws, including brackets for Grand Slam and 1000-level events, making it easy to keep track of matchups and results for each round.

Do you use Apple Sports? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
